target_customer: Families in Seattle area needing on-demand sitters
problem: Parents struggled to find trusted last-minute childcare.
business_model: Managed marketplace: Poppy vetted sitters, set hourly rates (about $16 per hour for one child per a 2016 report) and kept a margin

founders.name: Avni Patel Thompson
previous_startups: An earlier startup that did not work out
founders.background_notes: Named in GeekWire coverage seen only in search snippets (pages returned 403); background is from snippets, so education is null.

founders.name: Richerd Chan
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; page gives no background.

exit.reason: Company said it could not build a sustainable and scalable business model; it was hard to keep prices low for parents while paying caregivers fairly. Service stopped December 4, 2018 and the brand was taken over by The Baby Post.

technical_complexity.rationale: Text-message and app booking on top of a vetted sitter roster is simple software; the work was operations.

defensibility.rationale: Vetting and a local roster built trust but were replicable, and unit economics limited scale.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought it. Poppy shut in December 2018 and Sittercity and UrbanSitter were suggested to its families.

market_need_then: Founder story and local press describe frequent last-minute sitter needs. GeekWire (snippet) reports 36,000 bookings over about three years.

branding.domain_note: meetpoppy.com, a prefix domain, used throughout; redirects now to babypost.com.
branding.brand_signature: Text us when you need a sitter
branding.community_and_virality: Coverage said families loved the service and the shutdown story drew attention (GeekWire headline says rave-worthy service); a YC talk by the founder about shutting down exists.

brand_strength.rationale: Friendly name and a well-liked service, with local press in Seattle, but a regional brand. The Baby Post acquired the brand after closure, which suggests it kept some value.

outcome_analysis: Poppy delivered a popular managed childcare service and raised money from Madrona, YC and angels, but could not make the economics of vetted sitters work at venture growth rates. The company's own wording cites an unsustainable, unscalable model, and the founder described steady but modest monthly growth. It closed on 2018-12-04.
notes: GeekWire pages returned 403 and were read only through search snippets. Round stage not labeled by sources so stage is other. Totals conflict: Crosscut and GeekWire 2018 snippet say over 2 million raised, so earlier or later rounds are missing and not found. Competitors: UrbanSitter, Sittercity and Care.com are named in a GeekWire snippet and CB Insights, but I found no source dated at or near the 2016 batch, so the list is left empty rather than padded.
